finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> has no authentication or authorization; any unauthenticated caller can retrieve any invoice record by ID (IDOR / missing auth).
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP client supplying the inv_id path segment.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returning the full invoice record from INVOICES (invoices.py:10).

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) lookup with no caller identity check.
Entire invoice record serialized to response.

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, no login_required-style decorator, no g.user check, no ownership comparison, no token/signature on inv_id, no rate limiting in this file. Sibling /my/invoice route does enforce ownership, so omission appears unintentional. Severity depends on ID guessability and whether IDs are intended as capability tokens; population of INVOICES is not in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7-10 has no auth decorator, no ownership check, and no lookup filter. A grep of the directory finds no before_request/before_app_request hook, no login_required, and no assignment to g.user. The only related check is the sibling /my/invoice route at invoices.py:16-17, which does not apply to /invoice/<inv_id>.
verdict.reason: The route at invoices.py:7 returns the full INVOICES record for any inv_id (invoices.py:9-10) with no identity check, so an anonymous caller can read any invoice; the only caveat is that auth enforced outside this directory (e.g., a gateway or the unseen app setup) would be needed to refute it, and nothing in the provided code shows one.

finding.claim: Ownership checks on /my/invoice/<inv_id> and /my/invoices rely on g.user, which this file never sets and no auth middleware is present; the protection is only as strong as the unseen code that sets g.user. Unverified candidate.
finding.source: Not directly attacker-controlled in this file; trust derives from g.user['id'] (set outside this directory).
finding.sink: Ownership comparison inv['customer'] != g.user['id'] (invoices.py:16) and list filter (invoices.py:23).
finding.guards_checked: Ownership check at line 16 returns 404 for both not-found and not-owned (no existence oracle). No auth middleware in file. Within this file alone, g.user is undefined, producing a 500 rather than a bypass. Becomes a bypass only if the surrounding app sets g.user from client-controlled, unverified input (e.g., unsigned cookie/header). Not verifiable from this directory.

verdict.guard_found: Ownership check at invoices.py:16-17 (`inv["customer"] != g.user["id"]` then `abort(404)`) and the owner filter at invoices.py:23. No auth decorator or middleware exists in this file or elsewhere in the directory. The only directory contents are invoices.py and .claude/skills markdown files, so nothing in the directory sets g.user.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file (route decorators at lines 13 and 21, comparisons at lines 16 and 23), and the ownership check at invoices.py:16-17 is effective if g.user is trustworthy. Whether an attacker can spoof g.user depends on code outside this directory, which I cannot read, so the claim cannot be confirmed or refuted here. Separately, the unauthenticated /invoice/<inv_id> route at invoices.py:7-10 returns any invoice with no ownership check, which the candidate did not mention.
